candidate.answerReason: The quarter-turn creates an overlap that is a square of side 2.5 inches. Subtracting its area once from the sum of the two rectangle areas gives 30 − 6.25 = 23.75 square inches.

methods.label: Locate and subtract the overlap
methods.explanation:
Adding the two rectangle areas counts their common region twice, so first find the overlap. Let \(M\) be the midpoint of \(DC\). Since \(DC=AB=5\),
\[
DM=MC=2.5\text{ inches}.
\]
With \(DC\) horizontal and the original rectangle above it, the clockwise quarter-turn moves \(D\) to a point \(2.5\) inches above \(M\) and \(C\) to a point \(2.5\) inches below \(M\). The rotated rectangle extends \(3\) inches to the right of this new vertical side, because the original rectangle extended \(3\) inches above \(DC\).

The common region must lie to the right of \(M\) and above \(DC\). There, the original rectangle limits the width to \(MC=2.5\), while the rotated rectangle limits the height to \(2.5\). Each other dimension is \(3>2.5\), so the entire \(2.5\)-by-\(2.5\) square is shared.

Each rectangle has area \(5\cdot3=15\) square inches. Subtract the overlap once so that every covered part is counted once:
\[
15+15-2.5\cdot2.5
=30-6.25=23.75.
\]
The total covered area is \(23.75\) square inches, choice D.
